title: Spatial join + rates
query: zones.geojson holds 9 zones with a population field, and incidents.csv holds incident locations (lat/lon). Count the incidents in each zone and compute the rate per 1,000 residents. Which zone has the highest rate, and what is it?

expected_why.top_rate_per_1000: counts placed by construction, >= 60 m from any edge

answer:
I counted the incidents in each zone via a point-in-polygon spatial join (256 total incidents; 251 fell inside a zone, 5 were outside all zones) and computed the rate per 1,000 residents.

| Zone | Incidents | Population | Rate per 1,000 |
|------|-----------|------------|----------------|
| **Z2** | 19 | 830 | **22.89** |
| Z5 | 66 | 7,400 | 8.92 |
| Z1 | 41 | 5,200 | 7.88 |
| Z4 | 18 | 2,600 | 6.92 |
| Z6 | 25 | 3,900 | 6.41 |
| Z8 | 37 | 6,100 | 6.07 |
| Z7 | 9 | 1,500 | 6.00 |
| Z3 | 22 | 4,100 | 5.37 |
| Z9 | 14 | 2,800 | 5.00 |

**The zone with the highest rate is Z2, at 22.89 incidents per 1,000 residents.**

Note: Z2 has the highest *rate* despite having only the 6th-highest raw incident count (19) because its population is by far the smallest (830 residents). Z5 has the most incidents (66) but a much larger population (7,400), giving it a rate of 8.92.
